# PB-04 Stage A: borrowed projection deltas

Stage A is committed as `7e669e179e6cc726185ac80627a6bdca146944f1`.
PB-04 remains in progress. There is still no supported normal operating envelope
under the provisional budgets: full State loading, cloning, quota encoding and
snapshot persistence remain history-sensitive. The isolated rooted-state example
is a separate experiment and is not part of this production increment.

The PostgreSQL adapter now derives native/public projection deltas from borrowed
typed identities and fields. It normalizes duplicate row identities with the same
last-writer semantics as the old generator and avoids full JSON derivation for
unchanged source records. For changed public candidates it uses the existing
inspection sanitizers, including a conservative JSON comparison when source
fields differ but the public output may not. Only genuinely changed rows reach
the existing batched SQL writes. The old JSON implementation remains a test oracle.
No schema, ownership, protection, quota, public Storage API or event rule changes.

Four differential tests cover unchanged/materialized/removal paths, all native
index kinds, duplicate identities/aliases, effect kind collisions, redaction,
receipt offset shifts, cursors, scope changes and valid mutations of every
serialized Run field. The candidate passed 120 default workspace test executions,
31 executions in the PostgreSQL-enabled command and two administrative CLI
executions, plus strict workspace/all-target/all-feature Clippy and format checks.
Counts describe commands and include unit cases repeated by the PostgreSQL command.

The opt-in profiling run repeats the unchanged PB-02 full matrix, with five
artifacts, 24 samples per cell, histories 0/32/128/512, pending children,
concurrent admission, queue/fairness and five quota-refusal cases. At history 512,
mean CAS projection stage elapsed falls from PB-03's 18.104 ms to 5.142 ms;
subtracting measured SQL-driver time leaves about **4.357 ms**, compared with
17.185 ms before. Stage spans include SQL and CPU. Driver API calls are not wire
round trips; subtraction is an explanatory estimate, not a separate CPU profiler.
This reduces allocation/work while retaining O(H) scans and O(H) small map nodes,
plus changed-row JSON and the largest candidate temporary. It does not establish
O(W) persistence or fix full-state work.

Profiled event admission p95 is 13.985/18.501/45.913/125.948 ms for histories
0/32/128/512 against the unchanged 25 ms budget. The larger histories still fail.
Default-off full and reduced matrices are retained too. Their host load differs:
`projection-full` and `projection-minimal` were accidentally started concurrently;
`projection-full-sequential` had no concurrent operating-envelope matrix but did
overlap development of the separate prototype and its database/audit process.
These are explicitly shared-load observations, not a controlled speedup claim or
an attempt to qualify a tiny passing cell. Other agents also compiled/tested on
the host. Raw hardware, load averages, process time, source inventories, database
resource limits and durable PostgreSQL settings are retained for each experiment.
No supported capacity is inferred from any small finite passing point.

All PostgreSQL runs use new disposable containers pinned to PostgreSQL 17.11 image
`sha256:266d3c257594e195b309ae9d1805e54c788f1d7b375f56bf6c367aac6c917e7b`,
with two database CPUs, 1 GiB memory, 128 MiB shared memory, fsync,
synchronous_commit and full_page_writes enabled. The Rust release process runs
on the shared host, without a separate CPU/memory cgroup. No providers/services
other than this explicitly disposable PostgreSQL instance are used.

The `--state-costs` addition is an opt-in release-only CPU probe; default workloads
are unchanged. It measures exact canonical quota encoding, State/index cloning,
and serde Value encode/decode separately. Input Value cloning lies outside decode
timing. Raw results show full-state costs remain material at 512 histories; they
also retain the noisy 128-history host tail rather than normalizing it away.

Qualification files live under `.local/pb04/{checks,cpu-baseline,projection-profile,
projection-full,projection-minimal,projection-full-sequential}` and are copied to
the immutable Stage A evidence bundle listed in the companion JSON. The exact
47-file source archive for the profiled runtime includes all four committed Stage A
files with matching hashes. Later matrix source inventories may also list unused,
in-progress prototype example files; those files are not compiled into the
`operating_envelope` target. Their presence does not redefine the qualified
production diff.
